headline: Bangladesh plans to purchase Chinese J-10CE fighter jets and attack helicopters
summary: The government is moving forward with the acquisition to modernize the Air Force, citing the aircraft's performance and cost-effectiveness.
details: Prime Minister’s Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman announced that Bangladesh is moving ahead with plans to purchase Chinese J-10CE multirole fighter jets and attack helicopters to modernize the Bangladesh Air Force.

A committee has already held negotiations and a draft agreement has been prepared. The purchase will proceed this fiscal year if budget support is available; otherwise, it will be deferred to the next budget.

Zahed highlighted the J-10CE's reported performance, claiming it had downed a Dassault Rafale during a conflict between India and Pakistan, a point he noted as a key factor in the government's interest.
The adviser also stated that Chinese fighter jets are significantly more affordable than comparable European aircraft, such as the Rafale and the Eurofighter Typhoon.

Beyond the hardware, Zahed described the move as part of a "second independence," stating that Bangladesh is now more capable of making independent strategic decisions on foreign and defence policy based on its own interests.
He clarified that this "second independence" refers to the ability to make strategic choices, and should not be compared to the the country's struggle for independence in 1971.

headline: 907 hospitalised as 3 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll has risen to 88, with over 30,000 cases reported so far this year, according to the DGHS.
details: At least three dengue patients died and 907 others were hospitalised in the last 24 hours until 8:00am today.
Of the three deaths, two were reported in Dhaka South City Corporation and one in Dhaka division, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
With the new deaths and cases, the total number of dengue deaths has risen to 88, while the number of cases has reached 30,830.
Currently, 2,090 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at different hospitals across the country.
